purpose: App for reviewing personal writing and providing feedback and direction.
description: APT Local Novel Review Desktop App (V1): a local-first, review-only Electron + React + TypeScript + Vite desktop app in a pnpm workspace that imports .docx manuscripts as versions, parses them into chapters, runs structured review modes through a local Ollama model (gpt-oss:20b), persists projects, versions, chapters, review runs, and findings in SQLite (better-sqlite3), and compares findings across versions (resolved, still, new). Shared types, lib (parsing, schemas, prompts, compare), db (migrations and repositories), and ui packages support the desktop app.

architecture.summary: The renderer requests actions through window.aptApi; the preload forwards them over IPC; the Electron main process validates input, handles filesystem, SQLite, and Ollama calls, and returns typed payloads. Calls are one-way renderer -> preload -> main.
components: apps/desktop (@apt/desktop): Electron app with main (IPC handlers, runtime, review, versioning, and path services), a minimal preload API, and the React renderer pages (Setup, Library, import, review, findings, compare, settings, canon).
packages/lib (@apt/lib): DOCX parsing into chapters, Zod schemas for review results, Ollama prompt and client logic, hashing, and version compare logic, with unit tests.
packages/ui (@apt/ui): reusable UI components and tokens for the dark-first, card-based APT styling.
architecture.runtime_model: A Windows desktop Electron app. The main process talks to Ollama only at http://127.0.0.1:11434 and stores data in SQLite under %APPDATA%\@apt\desktop\apt-novel-reviewer (development uses a separate APT-Novel-Reviewer-Dev directory). contextIsolation is on, nodeIntegration is off, the renderer never calls Ollama directly, and CSP limits connections to the local Ollama endpoint.
architecture.deployment_model: Not a Cloudflare app. pnpm release:win builds an unsigned Windows 10 22H2+ x64 NSIS installer and SHA-256 checksum in release/ (ignored) with electron-builder; nothing is published and there are no automatic updates. Releases must be accepted on a clean Windows account or VM before sharing.

runtime.summary: Install Node 22 LTS and pnpm 9.12.1, run pnpm install (better-sqlite3 needs native tooling on Windows), start the desktop app with pnpm dev, and validate with typecheck, lint, and test. Reviews need a local Ollama with gpt-oss:20b, which the Setup page can install, start, and download on request.

constraints: This is a review tool, not a writing tool: do not add manuscript rewriting or editing features, and do not add chat assistant UI.
Keep the architecture local-first: no cloud APIs, cloud services, or telemetry by default; the Ollama endpoint is local only and manuscripts are sent only there.
Preserve the split between Electron main/preload and the React renderer; do not bypass the preload security boundary and keep calls one-way renderer -> preload -> main.
Every import creates a new manuscript version.
Review outputs must be strict, schema-validated JSON; validate external inputs and runtime contracts with Zod.
Default model for V1 is gpt-oss:20b; SQLite is the structured persistence layer.
Preserve manuscript and user content boundaries and do not invent review claims without source evidence.
Keep reusable review doctrine upstream in apt-principles-agents; local workflow decisions stay here.
UI follows APT: dark-first palette, card-based layouts, low visual noise, single accent focus, subtle motion only.
New logic should include unit tests where practical; keep modules small and single-purpose and avoid hidden global state.
Upgrades and uninstall must preserve project and manuscript data; uninstall does not remove Ollama or its models.
The local release is unsigned and has no automatic updates or publishing; only install builds from a trusted source.
Implementation order: app shell and runtime, project system, DOCX import and chapter parsing, SQLite persistence, Ollama review engine, findings and compare, remaining review modes and polish.
